Definition: from an obsolete verb akin to ἕπσω (to "steep"); cooked, i.e. roasted:--broiled.
BiblicalUsage: Broiled fish appears once, on the evening of the resurrection day, when the disciples gave the risen Jesus a piece of a broiled fish and of an honeycomb, and He took it and ate before them.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hold is that the broiled fish is the most ordinary proof of the resurrection: the risen Jesus was not a spirit, He ate in front of His friends.
